headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write files and uses shared state via Dify server datastore; marketingskills also reads/writes files and builds on shared context. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in one agent’s files or outputs can be treated as instructions by the other. No direct provenance controls are documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF either agent ingests shared files or shared context as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected through the Dify datastore or shared skill files, attacker text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Add provenance tags to all shared files.
Require explicit human review before executing file-derived instructions.
Disable automatic loading of shared context files.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content and conversation logs and has broad network egress; marketingskills reads/writes local skill files and can call GitHub/marketing-skills.com. If they share workspace or datastore, sensitive Dify content can flow into B’s outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not show hard isolation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or datastore, file contents can leak across them.
IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge base content are copied into marketingskills prompts, they may be transmitted to external sites.
mitigations: Keep separate storage buckets for each agent.
Redact secrets from shared prompts and files.
Turn off outbound calls for marketingskills during sensitive runs.
Review logs for cross-agent data flow.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and DLP.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and spawn subprocesses, and Dify additionally executes shell commands and writes the filesystem. If they operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or corrupt shared artifacts. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the overlap is a real default risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, file clobbering or partial writes can occur.
IF either agent modifies shared generated artifacts without locks, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on shared artifacts.
Check timestamps before overwriting files.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate agent/workflow outputs from tools, and marketingskills is explicitly a skill system that builds on shared context. That makes it plausible that B treats A’s output as authoritative without verification, causing errors to cascade into downstream marketing content or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes Dify-generated text as source material, mistakes can propagate.
IF either agent publishes or acts on unverified outputs from the other, downstream errors can multiply.
mitigations: Require a verification step before reuse.
Mark A-generated content as untrusted by default.
Compare outputs against source documents.
Limit automated downstream actions.
requires-engineering: add citation and confidence propagation.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, model-provider keys, and tool credentials, while marketingskills is a marketing-content skill set with no special regulated-data claims. The main issue is a potential retention or residency mismatch if sensitive Dify data is copied into B’s files or external calls. No direct regulated-data conflict is documented, so low fits.
conditions: IF regulated data from Dify is copied into marketingskills files or outbound requests, retention and residency obligations may be affected.
IF the operator uses these agents for EU PII or PHI without a DPA or equivalent controls, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of marketingskills inputs.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Use a DPA before sending personal data to external services.
Delete temporary files after each run.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
